subject: Post-demo recommended model shortlist & evaluation plan — Civitas
messages:
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@civitashealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Jan 2028 16:02:00 -0800
Subject: Post-demo recommended model shortlist & evaluation plan — Civitas

Hi Elena,

Thanks again for taking the time today — great dialogue and very helpful context on the triage / intake workload and the latency/cost constraints. Below is a concise post-demo recap, our recommended shortlist, and suggested next steps for the 2-week evaluation you asked about.

Quick recap of requirements you emphasized:
- P95 inference latency target: ~200 ms for single-turn triage calls
- Budget sensitivity: must keep hosted inference spend under ~$3k/month during pilot
- Data handling: PHI redaction before logging; customer-managed KMS for keys
- Quality: high recall on intent classification + conservative hallucination profile

Redwood recommended shortlist (high-level rationale):
1) RedSea-4 16B (distilled, fp16) — "Operational sweet spot"
   - Quality: strong for triage classification and short-form extraction
   - Latency: ~80–140 ms p95 on Dedicated small pool; ~160–260 ms on Hosted depending on batch tuning
   - Cost: lowest per-token of the shortlist; quantizes well for extra savings

2) Llama-3-70B (8k context, quantized) — "Quality-first fallback"
   - Quality: best quality on nuanced prompts and multi-step extraction; lower hallucination rate in our evaluations
   - Latency: ~180–350 ms p95 on Dedicated with optimized kernels; higher on shared Hosted tiers
   - Cost: mid-high; recommended as fallback for edge cases where recall matters

3) OpenLong-34B (long-context variant, fp16) — "Context-sensitive cases"
   - Quality: best when you need multi-turn context preserved across longer notes
   - Latency: higher p95; recommended only for workflows where context retention outweighs latency concerns

Benchmarks and artifacts shared (attached + Drive):
- latency_cost_matrix_q1-2028.csv (p50/p95 numbers across Hosted/Dedicated/Private)
- civitas_prompt_set_v2.json (anonymized prompt set with your example triage dialogs)
- eval_playbook_Civitas.pdf (detailed A/B plan, metrics we’ll track: recall, precision, hallucination rate, latency, cost)

Proposed 2-week evaluation plan (minimal friction):
- Week 0 (this week): RW sends config, prompt set, test harness + short onboarding call (30m)
- Week 1: run side-by-side on RedSea-4 (primary) vs Llama-3-70B (fallback) — measure p95, recall on your test set
- Week 2: tune batching, enable prefix caching for repeated prompts, run final perf/cost snapshot and an ops playbook review

Asks / decisions for Civitas to confirm:
- Can you share a de-identified sample of 500 triage cases (S3 link or secure Drive) for scoring?
- Confirm whether Hosted trial spend limit should be enforced at $3k (we can gate with rate limits)
- Who from your security/compliance team should be looped for the KMS integration?

If this matches your expectations I’ll schedule the kickoff call (30m) — proposed windows: Thu 1/12 10:00–11:00 PT or Fri 1/13 9:00–10:00 PT.

Thanks — I’ll leave Ben and Marissa on copy for technical/ops detail.

Best,
Aisha Rahman
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference
--
Attachments: civitas_prompt_set_v2.json, latency_cost_matrix_q1-2028.csv, eval_playbook_Civitas.pdf

From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@civitashealth.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Civitas Procurement <procurement@civitashealth.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Jan 2028 09:47:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo recommended model shortlist & evaluation plan — Civitas

Hi Aisha,

Really clear — appreciate the concise shortlist. A couple quick clarifications from our side:

1) Latency: the 200 ms p95 is a soft target for the triage quick-path (single-turn classification). For the longer extraction flows we can accept higher p95. Is the ~80–140 ms p95 number for RedSea-4 measured on Dedicated with a small GPU pool (1–2 GPUs) or on Hosted?

2) PHI redaction: we must ensure that PHI is removed before any logs leave our network. Is the KMS integration you referenced going to let us prevent plaintext logging?

3) Cost: $3k/mo cap works for the pilot but procurement will want a clear burn estimate and an exit plan if we need to stop the trial early. Please include a simple burn/run chart.

We can provide a de-identified sample by tomorrow morning; I’ll confirm who from Security should be on the KMS thread (likely Marcos Silva).

Thanks — Elena
Elena Ruiz
Head of Product, Care Coordination
CivitasHealth

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@civitashealth.com>, Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Jan 2028 11:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo recommended model shortlist & evaluation plan — Civitas

Elena — quick answers to the technical questions below, happy to jump on the kickoff call and walk through numbers.

On RedSea-4 latency: the 80–140 ms p95 number I quoted is from Dedicated (small pool, 1x A10 equivalent GPU with our optimized kernels, no batching). On Hosted (shared clusters), expect 140–260 ms p95 out of the box; we can usually push that down to ~120–180 ms with request-level batch hints and prefix caching turned on.

PHI / logging: yes — for the pilot we can do client-side redaction in a small middleware shim (we’ll share an example Lambda) so no PHI leaves your VPC. If you want Redwood Private with customer-managed KMS, we can disable request/response logging entirely at the control-plane and only store aggregated metrics. I’ve attached the KMS integration checklist in the Drive link.

Cost/burn: see attached latency_cost_matrix_q1-2028.csv for cost-per-1k-tokens estimates. Rough example for triage (avg 150 tokens / request, 10k requests/day):
- RedSea-4 (Dedicated): ~$2k/mo with conservative autoscale settings
- Llama-3-70B (fallback): incremental ~$1.2k/mo if used at 10% of traffic
We’ll provide a run chart for procurement before the kickoff.

Proposed evaluation A/B: primary = RedSea-4 (full traffic), fallback = Llama-3-70B for ~10% sampled cases flagged by confidence threshold. We’ll log pass/fail on recall and hallucination metrics to your Drive folder.

Links:
- Eval prompt set (anonymized): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1Civitas-EvalPack
- HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/REDWOOD/DEAL-2028-0842

If that looks good I can block time for a 30m kickoff Thursday (1/12) 10:00 PT.

—Ben
Principal Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference

Elena / Marcos — thanks for the quick replies and for confirming Marcos for security. Recap of agreed items and next steps so everyone has a single source of truth: 

Agreed / action items:
- Civitas: deliver de-identified sample (500 cases) to the Drive folder (link above) by EOD 1/11 — Elena said this is coming
- Redwood: provide client-side redaction Lambda example + onboarding checklist (Ben to send) — ETA: 1/13
- Redwood: run baseline benchmarks (RedSea-4 primary, Llama-3-70B fallback) and deliver run/burn chart to Procurement before kickoff — ETA: morning 1/13
- Kickoff: Thu 1/13 10:00 PT (Ben / Aisha / Marissa / Elena / Marcos) — Ben please confirm and send calendar invite

Evaluation plan for the call: we’ll walk through the prompt set, share initial p50/p95 numbers, and lock the success criteria (target recall, hallucination tolerance, and final cost cap for the pilot).

If procurement needs a quote doc for the pilot I can draft a short one-pager for signature/DocuSign.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this moving.

Best,
Aisha Rahman
